name: Google Scholar: archive objects as Scholar holds them
maxim: the index that reads the record is itself read
rule: One entry per Scholar cluster. Scholar's entry is kept as Scholar shows it (title, authors, date, description, truncated where Scholar truncates); beside it, the archive object it points at and that object's own fields, and a comparison of the two. A mismatch is recorded as data and does not block anything. Entries are added as the operator reports them or as they are observed, each with who observed it and when.
mechanism: Capture record pages (alexanarch.org/captures/<slug>/) carry citation_title, citation_author, citation_date and citation_public_url meta tags, which Google Scholar reads; Scholar takes the description from the record's finding (the registry's d field).

fields.scholar_url: the cluster link as Scholar gives it
fields.as_indexed: title, authors, date and description exactly as Scholar shows them
fields.object: the archive object the entry points at: url, kind, slug, and its own title, author, date, surface, sign-in state
fields.compared: field by field, whether Scholar's entry carries the object's value

as_indexed.title: who treated and constructed the semantic economy institute's entity?
as_indexed.description: METHOD TRACEABILITY, FIRST OBSERVATION. Asked who treated and constructed the Institute's entity, the composition resolves the method, its authorship, its date and the division of labour behind it, from five distinct sources. It separates the roles rather than collapsing them: Lee Sharks as institutional founder and archival authority, Rex Fraction as commercial voice and principal architect of the entity-construction methodology, with the SPXI Protocol authored under Fraction for the Institute in April 2026. It reaches the January 2026 institutional-provenance document, the Building Entities paper crediting both names and describing the Institute as a proof-of-concept entity constructed through that architecture, and the Wikidata work recorded under the Hauntedmemes account including the Institute item itself. Sources drawn: semanticeconomy. org (three times), spxi. dev, Mind Control Poems, TTGRS, Zenodo. And …
